title: axe select-name: six filter <select> elements have no accessible name
description: axe-core rule `select-name` (impact: critical), 6 instances across 4 tabs at runtime. Screen-reader users hear only "combo box" with no indication of what each filter does. Locations: MapExplorer.tsx:853 (species filter), :872 (county filter), :896 (media filter); SpeciesDetail.tsx:604 (county filter); LifeList.tsx:616 (county filter, the Multimedia tab); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376 (county filter). The visual label is a decorative MapPin icon with pointerEvents:'none', so nothing names the control. Checklists.tsx:629/:644 does this correctly with aria-label="Protocol"/"County" — that tab had zero select-name violations, proving the in-house fix pattern.
fix: Add aria-label to each select, matching the Checklists.tsx pattern: aria-label="Species filter" / "County" / "Media type" on the MapExplorer selects, and aria-label="County" on the SpeciesDetail, LifeList, and BreedingCodeList county selects.

verdict.reasoning: All six selects verified bare: MapExplorer 853/872/896 (SidebarLabel is an unassociated div), SpeciesDetail 604, LifeList 616, BreedingCodeList 376 (decorative MapPin only); grep confirms no aria-label/title on any of them, while Checklists.tsx 629/644 has the in-house aria-label fix. Accessible name computes to empty, so SR users hear only the current value with no control purpose — axe select-name at critical impact is fairly rated for six primary filter controls across four tabs. Minor imprecision only: for the three MapExplorer selects the visual label is the SidebarLabel div, not a MapPin icon.

title: Breeding-code badge contrast fails — in the exact category ACCESSIBILITY.md cites as exemplary (down to 1.71:1 in dark theme)
description: The statement says interface colors meet AA, 'for example, the top breeding-code badge uses dark text on its light tier color.' That is true only for the Breeding Codes table's tier-1 badge (BreedingCodeTable.tsx:219, #3B0764 on #C084FC = 5.68:1 light / 7.31:1 dark). Elsewhere the same badge concept fails: (1) ChecklistComparer's BreedingBadge uses `color: var(--sr-on-accent)` on `background: TIER_COLORS[def.tier]` — light theme: white on tier-1 #C084FC = 2.64:1; dark theme: #052E16 on tier-2 #A855F7 = 3.77:1, tier-3 #7C3AED = 2.62:1, tier-4 #6B21A8 = 1.71:1 (the badge text is essentially illegible in dark mode). (2) BreedingCodeTable.tsx:218-219 badge in dark theme: white on tier-2 #A855F7 = 3.96:1 (0.6875rem bold = small text, needs 4.5). (3) SpeciesDetail.tsx:788 breeding pill renders its label in TIER_COLORS[tier]; for tier 1 in light theme that is #C084FC on a near-white 8%-tinted surface ≈ 2.6:1. The published example claim is materially false outside the one table.
fix: In ChecklistComparer, reuse the BreedingCodeTable pattern: per-tier text color (`--sr-tier-1-text` on tier 1, white on tiers 3-4) instead of --sr-on-accent, and add a dark-theme tier-2 text token (white on #A855F7 fails; #1A0030-style dark text passes at ~4.97:1); for the SpeciesDetail pill, use the darker tier-text token rather than the raw tier color for tier 1.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all ratios with WCAG luminance: ChecklistComparer's BreedingBadge fails in both themes (light tier-1 white-on-#C084FC = 2.64:1; dark #052E16 on tier-2/3/4 = 3.77/2.62/1.71) at 0.625rem bold small text, and the BreedingCodeTable dark tier-2 (3.96) and SpeciesDetail tier-1 pill (2.46 on the composited 8% surface) sub-claims also verify. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 31 holds the breeding badge up as the AA example and its only disclosed exception is chart-bar labels, so this is not disclosed. Serious is correct: 1.71:1 on confirmed-breeding codes in dark mode is effectively illegible and contradicts the published statement.
verdict.fixNote: Per the tokens-in-both-themes convention, define per-tier text tokens rather than branching inline: keep --sr-tier-1-text (exists in both themes), add --sr-tier-2-text (#FFFFFF in :root = 5.38:1 on #9333EA; #1A0030 in dark = 4.88:1 on #A855F7) and --sr-tier-3-text/--sr-tier-4-text (#FFFFFF both themes, 5.70–15.0:1). Export a TIER_TEXT_COLORS map alongside TIER_COLORS in lib/breedingCodes.ts and use it in ChecklistComparer's BreedingBadge AND BreedingCodeTable.tsx:219 (whose hardcoded '#fff' also violates the no-raw-hex rule). For the SpeciesDetail.tsx:789 pill, set the tier-1 label color to var(--sr-tier-1-text) instead of the raw tier color.

title: Contrast claim is overstated: informational text rendered in the --sr-text-disabled token sits at 2.3–2.6:1 in both themes
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md claims body text and primary interface text meet 4.5:1 in both themes, with exactly one disclosed exception (percentage labels inside chart bars). In fact, real informational text — not disabled controls — is rendered in --sr-text-disabled, which computes to 2.56:1 light (#A1A1AA on #FFFFFF) / 2.45:1 on the page bg, and 2.29:1 dark (#52525B on #18181B). Locations: Checklists.tsx:177 and :668 (the result-count labels that are also the polite live regions), MediaCommentsSection.tsx:100 and NamedBirdsTable.tsx:77 (count labels), SpeciesDetail.tsx:461 ('{n} species' count) and :584 (scientific names inside the species-combobox options), ChecklistComparer.tsx:534 (italic placeholder labels), and the uppercase mini-headers in SetupRequired.tsx:56, ListComparer.tsx:203, HelpDocs.tsx:354. None of these are covered by the statement's disclosed chart-label exception, so the published claim is false as written, and low-vision users genuinely cannot read these labels.
fix: Use --sr-text-muted (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark — already passing) for all informational text and reserve --sr-text-disabled strictly for genuinely disabled controls; or add a passing 'faint text' token. Then re-verify the ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast paragraph.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran WCAG luminance math: --sr-text-disabled is 2.56:1 on white / 2.46:1 on --sr-surface-faint (the line 177/668 labels' actual backdrop) light, 2.29:1 / 2.20:1 dark — all well below 4.5:1 for 11-12px informational text. All ten cited locations exist and use the token for real content (count labels that are also the only result-count display, combobox sci names, mini-headers), and ACCESSIBILITY.md's sole disclosed exception (chart-bar percentage labels) covers none of them, so the published AA claim is false as written. Fix is correct and convention-compliant: --sr-text-muted passes in both themes (4.83/4.63 light, 6.91/6.63 dark) and is already defined in both.

title: Filter form controls have no programmatic label across most data tabs
wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (also 2.4.6) AA
description: The county <select> and From/To date inputs are repeated across tabs with no aria-label, no <label for>, and no association to any visible text — a screen-reader user hears an unnamed combobox and two unnamed, indistinguishable date fields. Locations: LifeList.tsx:616 (county select), :644 and :658 (date from/to); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376, :408, :424 (same trio); SpeciesDetail.tsx:604, :629, :643 (same trio). Related instances where a VISIBLE label exists but is not programmatically associated: MapExplorer.tsx:853 (species select), :872 (county select), :896 (media select) and :862/:864 (date text inputs) — their 'Species'/'County'/'Media'/'Date Range' headings are SidebarLabel <div>s (map/MapSidebarUI.tsx:35-43), so the selects have no accessible name and the two free-text date inputs are distinguishable only by the placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD' (format instruction also vanishes once filled — 3.3.2); Settings.tsx:1214, :1226, :1238 (Latitude/Longitude/Radius number inputs whose labels are plain <div>s at :1213/:1225/:1237); ChecklistComparer.tsx:350-353 ('Checklist A/B' <label> elements with no htmlFor, so the inputs' name falls back to the example-URL placeholder). Checklists.tsx:629-663 does this correctly (aria-label="Protocol"/"County"/"From date"/"To date"), proving the house pattern exists.
fix: Match the Checklists.tsx pattern: add aria-label ("County", "From date", "To date") to the bare selects/date inputs in LifeList, BreedingCodeList, SpeciesDetail. In MapExplorer, render SidebarLabel as a <label htmlFor> (or add aria-label to each control), and give the two date inputs distinct names ("Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)"). In Settings, convert the Latitude/Longitude/Radius caption <div>s to <label htmlFor> with input ids. In ChecklistComparer, add htmlFor/id to the existing <label> elements.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every cited location in current code: LifeList/BreedingCodeList/SpeciesDetail county selects and date inputs have no aria-label/label/title; MapExplorer's SidebarLabel is a bare <div> (MapSidebarUI.tsx:35-43) so its selects are unnamed and the two text date inputs share the identical 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder; Settings lat/lon/radius captions are plain <div>s; ChecklistComparer's <label> has no htmlFor and doesn't wrap the input. Checklists.tsx really does carry the aria-label house pattern the fix cites, and ACCESSIBILITY.md discloses only chart-label contrast as a known exception, not this. Serious is the right severity — repeated unnamed form controls across most data tabs is a genuine 4.1.2/1.3.1 SR barrier, though the controls remain operable.
verdict.fixNote: The fix is correct and convention-consistent (mirror Checklists.tsx's aria-label="County"/"From date"/"To date"). One caveat: do not unconditionally convert SidebarLabel to <label htmlFor> — it also captions the Breeding Code SegControl, a button group with no labelable element. Either add aria-label per control in MapExplorer (including format-bearing names like 'Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)' on the free-text date inputs), or give SidebarLabel an optional htmlFor prop that renders <label> only when an id is passed.

title: Selected state not programmatically exposed on segmented controls and toggle pills
description: The shared SegControl renders plain <button>s whose active option is conveyed only by background/border/font-weight — no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radiogroup semantics. It is used for the Map Explorer radius (MapExplorer.tsx:700), breeding filter (:881), Pins/Heatmap display mode (:912), and All/Week (:1285). The same style-only-state defect appears in SpeciesDetail.tsx:1189 (Pins/Heatmap map-mode buttons), BirdingStats.tsx:541 (accumulation granularity), :1628 (breeding filter pills), :1717 (media view mode), ListComparer.tsx:215 (My List / Upload source buttons), and MapExplorer.tsx:1030 (hotspot kind-legend toggles, whose only state cue is opacity 0.4). A screen-reader user cannot tell which option is active. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md: "Filter pills announce whether they are pressed." The codebase already has the correct pattern (SortSeg in Checklists.tsx:74, SnowMap.tsx:144, SpeciesDetail graph groups :962/:974).
fix: Add aria-pressed={value === opt.value} (or role="radio"/aria-checked inside a role="radiogroup") to SegControl's buttons and to each listed location; wrap each group in role="group" with an aria-label.

verdict.reasoning: SegControl (MapSidebarUI.tsx:15-29) renders plain buttons with style-only active state, and every cited usage checks out: MapExplorer 700/881/912/1285, SpeciesDetail ~1189, BirdingStats 541/1628/1717, ListComparer 215, and the hotspot kind-legend toggles at MapExplorer 1030 whose only state cue is opacity 0.4. The correct pattern does exist in SortSeg (Checklists.tsx, role=group + aria-pressed) and SnowMap.tsx:144, and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'filter pills announce whether they are pressed' claim is contradicted rather than disclosed as an exception. Serious is fair: a screen-reader user cannot determine the active option on roughly ten primary filter/view controls.
verdict.fixNote: Give SegControl an ariaLabel prop rendered as role="group" aria-label on its wrapper div plus aria-pressed={value === opt.value} on each button, mirroring SortSeg in Checklists.tsx (the SidebarLabel above it is not programmatically associated, so the group needs its own label). Apply the same aria-pressed to the inline groups in SpeciesDetail, BirdingStats, and ListComparer; for the kind-legend visibility toggles use aria-pressed={!isHidden} so pressed means shown.

title: Inline error messages are silent to assistive tech (no role=alert/aria-live, no aria-describedby)
description:
Several async form-submission error paths render a plain styled
//

, so a screen-reader user who activates the control hears nothing and must hunt the page to discover the failure. Locations: MapExplorer.tsx:105 (place-name search failure), :687 (geolocation error), :1006-1011 (Find Hotspots error), :1227-1232 (Find Recent Sightings error); Settings.tsx:300-309 (malformed/failed CSV upload error in FileRow), :476-485 (API-key save error in KeyRow), :1210 (map-location detect error), :1281-1283 (map defaults save error — additionally the text 'Check your values and try again.' does not identify which of the three fields is invalid); ListComparer.tsx:276-280 (my-list load error). None are associated to their input via aria-describedby either. The codebase has correct reference implementations: App.tsx:668+717-736 (role=alert plus aria-describedby on the input), ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, DropZone.tsx:132, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:184.
fix: Give each error container role="alert" (or aria-live="polite" for non-urgent ones), and where the error relates to a specific input add id + aria-describedby on that input (the App.tsx checklist-input pattern). Make the map-defaults message name the offending field, e.g. "Latitude must be between -90 and 90."

verdict.reasoning: Every cited location verified as a plain styled div/span/p (MapExplorer 105/687/1006/1227, Settings 300-309/476-485/1210/1281-1283 including the field-anonymous 'Check your values' message, ListComparer 276-280); grep shows zero role=alert or aria-live in those files. The cited correct reference implementations all exist (App.tsx role=alert + aria-describedby, ChecklistComparer 372, DropZone 132, WeatherTidePanel 184), so this is inconsistent application of an established house pattern. Serious is fair for 4.1.3/3.3.1: async failures on key flows (location search, CSV upload, API-key save) are completely silent to SR users.

title: --sr-text-disabled used for real content text (2.29–2.56:1)
description: The disabled-text token (#A1A1AA light = 2.56:1 on surface, 2.45:1 on bg; #52525B dark = 2.29:1 on surface, 1.93:1 on surface-subtle) is widely used for meaningful, non-disabled content: Settings file sublabels (Settings.tsx:240) and full explanatory paragraphs (Settings.tsx:1143, 1174), file dates (:235), tab-layout 'HIDDEN' labels (:739), Species Detail counters and zero values (SpeciesDetail.tsx:461, 584, 690, 830, 926), comparer '—' and italic placeholders that convey 'no value' (ChecklistComparer.tsx:100, 534), the List Comparer section label (ListComparer.tsx:203), and the LifeList 'no filter' chip (LifeList.tsx:606). The WCAG inactive-control exemption does not apply to any of these — they are informative text.
fix: Replace --sr-text-disabled with --sr-text-muted (4.83:1 light / 6.91:1 dark on surface) everywhere the text is content rather than a label inside a genuinely disabled control; reserve the disabled token for disabled buttons/inputs only.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran the WCAG math independently: every reported ratio is exact (light #A1A1AA on #FFFFFF = 2.56:1, on #F9FAFB = 2.45:1; dark #52525B on #18181B = 2.29:1, on #27272A = 1.93:1; muted = 4.83/6.91 on surface). The cited Settings.tsx sites (235, 240, 250, 388, 739, 1143, 1174) are informative content — file dates, sublabels, status chips, explanatory paragraphs — none inside a disabled control, so the 1.4.3 inactive-control exemption does not apply. ACCESSIBILITY.md's contrast section claims AA for body text and discloses only chart-bar labels, not this; serious is the right severity for sub-2.6:1 body-size content text.
verdict.fixNote: Swapping to --sr-text-muted is right for most sites, but light-theme muted (#71717A) on --sr-surface-subtle (#F4F4F5) is only 4.40:1 — just under AA. The 'No file saved' / 'No key saved' chips (Settings.tsx:250, 388) sit on surface-subtle, so for those either use --sr-text (or a new AA-checked token added to BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css) or lighten the chip background; all other cited Settings sites are on --sr-surface or --sr-bg where muted passes (4.83:1 / 4.62:1 light, 6.91:1+ dark).

title: Filter selects and date inputs have no accessible name on four tabs
description: The county <select> and the From/To <input type="date"> controls have no aria-label, no <label>, and no title — a screen reader announces an unnamed combo box / date field. Same defect repeats: LifeList.tsx:616 (select), :645, :659 (dates); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376 (select), :409, :425 (dates); MapExplorer.tsx:853 (Species select), :872 (County select), :896 (Media select) — the visual SidebarLabel is a styled <div> with no htmlFor association — and MapExplorer.tsx:862/:864 (two date text inputs distinguished only by placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD"). Checklists.tsx:629/:644/:655/:663 does this correctly (aria-label on each), proving the intended pattern exists in-repo.
fix: Add aria-label to each control matching the Checklists tab pattern (aria-label="County", "From date", "To date", "Species", "Media"), or convert SidebarLabel to a <label htmlFor> association in MapExplorer.

verdict.reasoning: Every cited location verified: unnamed selects at SpeciesDetail.tsx:604, LifeList.tsx:616, BreedingCodeList.tsx:376, and MapExplorer.tsx:853/:872/:896 where SidebarLabel (map/MapSidebarUI.tsx:35) is a plain styled <div> with no htmlFor; MapExplorer.tsx:862/:864 are text inputs distinguished only by identical 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholders. Minor nit: HTML-AAM makes the placeholder a fallback accessible name on the two text inputs, but both compute to the same string so the fields remain indistinguishable, and the selects have no name at all. Serious is fair and the aria-label fix matches the existing Checklists.tsx pattern.

title: axe label: From/To date inputs on three tabs have no accessible name
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A (also 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions A)
description: axe-core rule `label` (impact: critical), 6 instances across 3 tabs at runtime. The date-range filter inputs are announced as unlabeled date fields, and the only visual relationship cue is a decorative Calendar icon and a "→" span. Locations: SpeciesDetail.tsx:630 and :644, LifeList.tsx:645 and :659 (Multimedia tab), BreedingCodeList.tsx:409 and :425. The identical control in Checklists.tsx:655/:663 carries aria-label="From date"/"To date" and passed — the fix pattern already exists in the codebase.
fix: Copy the Checklists.tsx pattern: add aria-label="From date" / aria-label="To date" to both date inputs in SpeciesDetail.tsx, LifeList.tsx, and BreedingCodeList.tsx.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: both date inputs at SpeciesDetail.tsx:629-654 and the LifeList.tsx/BreedingCodeList.tsx duplicates have no aria-label, <label>, or title, while Checklists.tsx:655/:663 carries the exact labels claimed. Real 4.1.2/3.3.2 failure — a SR user gets two identical unnamed date fields and cannot tell From from To. Downgraded critical→serious: 'critical' is axe's rule-impact taxonomy, but contextually these are secondary filter controls that stay operable, the same defect class finding 5 rates serious; the suggested fix is correct and matches the in-repo convention.

title: No h1, most views have no headings, and heading levels are inconsistent across tabs
description: The app title "SnowRaven" is styled <span>s in a <div> (App.tsx:570-580) — no h1 and no banner landmark. Settings, Life List, Species Detail, and Map Explorer contain no heading elements at all (section titles like "Appearance"/"Map Overlays" are styled divs), so SR heading navigation lands on nothing in four major views. Where headings do exist they are inconsistent: ListComparer.tsx:184 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:340 use h1 inside tab content while Checklists.tsx:522, BirdingStats.tsx:424 and NamedBirds.tsx:128 use h2; SetupRequired.tsx:31 (the empty state of 8 tabs) styles its title as a div. Additionally the main nav loses its landmark: role="tablist" on the <nav> (TabNav.tsx:105-108) overrides the navigation role, and in dropdown mode there is no nav element at all.
fix: Make the app title an h1 inside a <header>; give every tab view an h2 and section cards h3 (Settings/LifeList/SpeciesDetail/MapExplorer sidebar sections); make SetupRequired's title an h2; demote the comparer h1s to h2.

verdict.reasoning: All claims check out: the title is styled spans in a div (App.tsx:570-580, no h1/header element); grep shows zero heading elements in Settings, LifeList, SpeciesDetail, MapExplorer and SetupRequired (title is a styled div, SetupRequired.tsx:31); ListComparer:184/ChecklistComparer:340 use h1 in tab content while Checklists:522/BirdingStats:424/NamedBirds:128 use h2; TabNav.tsx:105-108 puts role="tablist" on the <nav> (killing the navigation landmark) and the dropdown variant renders no nav at all. Heading navigation is a primary SR strategy and four major views expose nothing, so this is genuinely user-impacting at 1.3.1 Level A; moderate is the right tier since tablist/main/contentinfo landmarks still give a navigation path.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested heading plan is sound (h1 title in <header>, h2 per view incl. SetupRequired, h3 section cards — statsPrimitives.tsx already uses h3 for stats cards, so follow that pattern), but it omits the landmark half of its own description: also move role="tablist" off the <nav> in TabNav.tsx onto an inner div so the navigation landmark survives, and wrap the dropdown-mode trigger+listbox in the same <nav aria-label="Main navigation">.

title: In-page jump links scroll the view but never move keyboard focus
description: The Statistics "Jump to section" nav (9 anchors) calls e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and LifeList's "media comments" anchor does the same (LifeList.tsx:505). preventDefault suppresses the browser's native sequential-focus relocation for fragment navigation, and the scroll targets are plain divs without tabindex="-1" (e.g. MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40), so after "jumping" a keyboard user's focus is still on the link at the top — the next Tab continues from the nav and they must traverse every control between anyway. The jump feature is effectively visual-only for keyboard users.
fix: After scrolling, move focus to the destination: give each section container tabindex={-1} and call el.focus({ preventScroll: true }) alongside smoothScrollIntoView (wrap in the existing scroll helper so all jump links inherit it).

verdict.reasoning: BirdingStats.tsx:449 (and LifeList.tsx:505) call e.preventDefault() + smoothScrollIntoView, and lib/scroll.ts only scrolls — it never moves focus; the targets are plain divs (SectionCard in statsPrimitives.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx:40) with no tabindex. preventDefault suppresses the browser's native fragment-navigation focus relocation, so after a jump the next Tab resumes from the nav chip — the feature is visual-only for keyboard users. The suggested fix (tabindex=-1 on targets + focus({preventScroll:true}) folded into the shared scroll helper) is correct and convention-conforming.
verdict.fixNote: Put tabIndex={-1} on the SectionCard root div (statsPrimitives.tsx) so all nine Statistics targets inherit it, add the same to the #media-comments div in MediaCommentsSection.tsx, and add a jumpTo(el) wrapper in lib/scroll.ts that calls smoothScrollIntoView(el) then el.focus({ preventScroll: true }); switch the three preventDefault call sites (BirdingStats.tsx:449, LifeList.tsx:505) to it. Add :focus-visible-only outline styling (or outline: none on [tabindex="-1"]) so the programmatic focus doesn't paint the green focus ring on the whole card for mouse users.

title: ChecklistBadges convey present/absent state via aria-label on generic spans; group unnamed
description: Each Badge is a role-less <span aria-label={presentTitle|absentTitle}>. ARIA prohibits naming on the generic role, and screen readers inconsistently honor aria-label on plain spans in browse mode — so SR users may hear only the visible "Photo Audio Video Breeding Weather Tide" text with the present/absent state (the badge's entire point) dropped. The wrapping role="group" (:53) also has no accessible name. The tests assert the aria-labels exist but can't catch the exposure problem.
fix: Add role="img" to the Badge span (making the aria-label valid and reliably announced), and aria-label="Checklist contents" on the role="group" container.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at ChecklistBadges.tsx:22-24 the Badge is a role-less span whose aria-label (prohibited on role=generic, inconsistently exposed by SRs) is the sole programmatic carrier of present/absent state — both states announce identically when it is dropped — and the role="group" at line 53 is indeed unnamed. Not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md (only the chart-bar contrast exception is). The suggested fix matches the codebase's own established pattern (Checklists.tsx:276 Badge uses role="img" aria-label; Checklists.tsx:69 names its role="group"), so it stands as-is.

title: Media count badges in checklist comparer use aria-label on a generic <span> — info silently lost to screen readers
description: MediaIcons renders per-species photo/audio/video presence as lucide SVG icons inside a plain <span aria-label={`${n} ${label}`}>. ARIA prohibits naming on role=generic, so most browser/SR pairs ignore the aria-label, and the SVGs themselves have no text alternative — the media information (which types exist and counts) is conveyed to sighted users only. The same file's Checklists tab equivalent (Checklists.tsx:276 Badge) does this correctly with role="img", and ChecklistBadges.tsx is correct too — this one component missed the pattern.
fix: Add role="img" to the span (matching the Badge pattern in Checklists.tsx:276) so the aria-label is exposed: <span role="img" aria-label={`${n} ${label}`} ...>.

verdict.reasoning: ChecklistComparer.tsx:57 puts aria-label on a bare span (role generic, where ARIA prohibits naming, so exposure is unreliable) wrapping lucide SVGs that carry no text alternative; no other text path in SideCell conveys media presence or counts. The repo's own correct pattern exists at Checklists.tsx:275 (Badge with role="img" aria-label), confirming this component missed it. Moderate is right: real informational content (a headline comparer data point) with no reliable SR exposure, but not a control or blocker.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested role="img" fix is correct and matches the in-repo Badge pattern; while there, reuse the already-built pluralized text for the name so SR output matches the tooltip: <span role="img" aria-label={`${n} ${label.toLowerCase()}${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`}> (the current aria-label would announce '2 Photo').

title: One-shot buttons unmount on activation, dropping keyboard focus to <body>
description: Repeated pattern: a focused control disappears when activated, resetting focus to the document body so the keyboard user's next Tab restarts from the top of the page. Locations: 'Show all N' one-shot buttons rendered behind `{!showAll && ...}` — Checklists.tsx:205 (comments) and :718 (checklist rows), MediaCommentsSection.tsx:159, SpeciesDetail.tsx:1347 (species comments); and Settings KeyRow Save/Cancel — Settings.tsx:457 (Cancel) and the post-save `setEditing(false)` at :973 unmount the editing row that contains the focused button. (The toggle-style variants that stay mounted — SpeciesDetail locations/co-occurrence, BirdingStats counties — are fine and are the model to copy.)
fix: Either keep the button mounted as a toggle ('Show fewer'), or on activation move focus explicitly — e.g. focus the first newly revealed row, or for KeyRow focus the Edit button that replaces the editor.

verdict.reasoning: ShowAllButton at Checklists.tsx:205 and :718 renders behind {!showAll && ...} and its onClick flips that state, unmounting the focused button; the file contains no useRef or .focus() call, so focus falls to <body> and the next Tab restarts from the page top. The same pattern is real at MediaCommentsSection.tsx:159, SpeciesDetail.tsx:1347, and Settings KeyRow (Cancel :457, post-save setEditing(false) :973). The toggle variants cited as the model do exist in-repo, so the fix direction matches existing conventions.
verdict.fixNote: Prefer the stay-mounted toggle ('Show fewer'), matching the existing in-repo model (SpeciesDetail locations/co-occurrence, BirdingStats counties). If moving focus instead, note the revealed rows are plain divs: give the first newly revealed row container tabIndex={-1} and call .focus() on it after the state flip (e.g. via a ref + effect keyed on showAll); for Settings KeyRow, focus the Edit button that replaces the editor.

title: Placeholder-only (or format-only) accessible names on text inputs; Map Explorer From/To dates are indistinguishable
wcag: 2.4.6 Headings and Labels AA / 1.3.1 Info and Relationships A
description: Several inputs have no label or aria-label, so the accessible name falls back to the placeholder. Worst case: the Map Explorer date-range inputs (MapExplorer.tsx:862,864) both have placeholder "YYYY-MM-DD" — a SR user hears the format string twice with nothing distinguishing From vs To (the visible "Date Range" SidebarLabel is not programmatically associated). Same pattern: MapExplorer.tsx:84 (place search), 689/691 (Latitude/Longitude), 1182 (target species search); Settings.tsx:1216/1228/1240 map-default inputs, whose visible "Latitude"/"Longitude"/"Radius (mi)" labels are unassociated <div>s so the computed name is "e.g. 37.8275"; SpeciesDetail.tsx:1268 and MediaCommentsSection.tsx:70 comment filters (placeholder is at least descriptive there, but disappears once text is typed for sighted users). Contrast: Checklists.tsx:655/663 date inputs do it right with aria-label="From date"/"To date".
fix: Add aria-label to each (e.g. "From date (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "To date (YYYY-MM-DD)", "Latitude", "Longitude", "Search by place name"), or associate the existing visible labels via htmlFor/id.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every cited input: MapExplorer 862/864 are both placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" with the 'Date Range' SidebarLabel an unassociated div, so From and To compute identical accessible names; 84, 689/691, 1182, Settings 1216/1228/1240 (visible Latitude/Longitude/Radius labels are plain divs), SpeciesDetail 1268, and MediaCommentsSection 70 all have placeholder-only names. Checklists.tsx 655/663 confirmed as the in-house aria-label="From date"/"To date" pattern the fix mirrors. Moderate is right — placeholders provide a partial name fallback, but the indistinguishable date pair is a genuine 2.4.6/1.3.1 failure.

title: Map Explorer async error messages are silent to assistive tech
description: The hotspot search error (:1006-1011) and media-targets search error (:1227-1232) render as plain styled divs after an async failure — no role="alert" or aria-live, so a screen-reader user who pressed "Find Hotspots"/"Find Recent Sightings" gets no feedback that the request failed (the role="status" loading chip just disappears). Other error paths in the app do this correctly (ChecklistComparer.tsx:372, App.tsx:720, DropZone.tsx:132).
fix: Add role="alert" to both error divs (matching ChecklistComparer's pattern).

verdict.reasoning: Verified: hotspotsError (1006-1011) and targetsError (1227-1232) render as plain divs with an aria-less AlertCircle icon, no role/aria-live anywhere in MapExplorer per grep, and the role=status loading chip (1437) simply unmounts on failure — so an SR user gets no failure feedback. Cited reference implementations (ChecklistComparer 372, App 720, DropZone 132) all exist, and role=alert on these two divs is the correct house-pattern fix. Note this is a strict subset of finding 11 (same two MapExplorer locations); confirmed independently at moderate, but the two should be deduplicated when applying fixes.

title: Placeholder is the only label on search/filter, coordinate, and API-key text inputs
description: These text inputs have no label or aria-label; their only identification is the placeholder, which disappears as soon as the user types (and browsers' placeholder→accessible-name fallback is a last resort, not a reliable label). Locations: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-70 ('Filter media comments…'); Checklists.tsx:161-165 (shared CommentSearchBox, placeholders 'Filter checklist comments…' / 'Filter species comments…' at :544/:555); SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1268 ('Filter comments…'); MapExplorer.tsx:82-84 ('Search by place name'), :689/:691 (Latitude/Longitude number inputs — after entry a sighted user sees two bare numbers with nothing saying which is which), :1182-1184 ('Search species…'); Settings.tsx:424-428 (API key entry, 'Paste your API key' — the row label at :352 is an unassociated <div>). Impact is worst for low-vision and cognitive users mid-entry, and for the lat/lng pair where the only differentiator vanishes.
fix: Add aria-label to each input (e.g. aria-label="Filter media comments", aria-label="Latitude", aria-label="eBird API key") while keeping the placeholder as a hint; for the Map Explorer lat/lng pair, prefer small visible labels like the Settings map-defaults section already has.

verdict.reasoning: Read every cited input: MediaCommentsSection.tsx:66-79, the shared CommentSearchBox in Checklists.tsx:161-175 (both instantiations), SpeciesDetail.tsx:1264-1277, MapExplorer.tsx:82-89/:689-692/:1182-1185, and Settings.tsx:424-440 — none has an aria-label, aria-labelledby, or associated <label>; the placeholder is the only identification, and the Settings row label is an unassociated <div>. ACCESSIBILITY.md's only disclosed exception is chart-bar contrast, so this is undisclosed. Moderate is correct: placeholder fallback usually yields *some* accessible name, but it vanishes on input (worst for the bare lat/lng number pair, which affects sighted users too) — a fair 3.3.2 AA failure, not serious, not pedantry.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested aria-labels are right and match the file-local convention (Checklists.tsx already puts aria-label on its Protocol/County selects and From/To date inputs; MapExplorer/Settings use aria-label heavily elsewhere). One refinement: CommentSearchBox is a shared component, so add a single aria-label derived from its existing title/placeholder prop (e.g. aria-label={placeholder.replace(/…$/, '')}) — one change covers both Checklists instances. For Settings, derive it from the row's label prop (aria-label={`${label} API key value`} or similar) rather than a hardcoded string, since the component renders multiple key rows.

title: List Comparer summary bars and result panels don't reflow at 320px — labels truncate to identical text
description: Both comparer results screens use rigid column counts with no narrow-width collapse. The five-cell summary (`gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(5, 1fr)'` — ResultsView.tsx:111 and ChecklistComparer.tsx:281) gives each cell ~58px at 320px; the 0.625rem uppercase labels are `whiteSpace: nowrap; overflow: hidden; textOverflow: ellipsis` (ResultsView.tsx:165-173, ChecklistComparer.tsx:478), so "Checklist A" and "Checklist B" (and "<name> total" pairs) ellipsize to identical strings — the numbers become indistinguishable at that width. Below them, ResultsView.tsx:129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` species panels and ChecklistComparer.tsx:310 `1fr 1fr` A-only/B-only panels never stack, leaving ~90-140px columns where species names wrap to 4+ lines. Nothing scrolls two-dimensionally and the panel headers repeat the counts, so it is degraded rather than lost — but the summary labels' ambiguity is a concrete information loss at 320px.
fix: Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` for the stat bars (cells wrap to two rows on narrow screens), and collapse the panel grids to one column under 640px (reuse the `.sr-two-col` media-query pattern from globals.css:601).

verdict.reasoning: Verified all cited lines: ResultsView.tsx:111 `repeat(5, 1fr)` with nowrap/ellipsis 0.625rem labels (165-176), :129 `repeat(3, 1fr)` panels, and the ChecklistComparer twins (281, 310, ~479) — all inline styles with zero responsive handling (no matchMedia, no media-query class) anywhere in ResultsView/ListComparer/ChecklistComparer. At 320px each stat cell is ~55-64px with 40px horizontal padding, leaving ~15-24px for the label (1-3 chars + ellipsis): 'Checklist A'/'Checklist B' and filename-derived labels (eBird exports share the 'MyEBirdData' prefix) truncate to identical strings — concrete information loss under SC 1.4.10, though the both/A-only/B-only counts are duplicated in the panel headers so only the two totals become truly ambiguous. Moderate is the right severity: real AA failure at 320px/400% zoom, but degraded rather than blocking.
verdict.fixNote: The stats-bar half of the fix is sound (rem-based `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(7rem, 1fr))` inline also scales with the in-app Text Size control). The panel half won't work as written: the grids' `gridTemplateColumns` are inline styles, and a media-query class rule cannot override an inline declaration — move the grid definition into a class (as SpeciesDetail.tsx:802 uses `className="sr-two-col"` with no inline grid). ResultsView's panel grid is 3 columns, so `.sr-two-col` isn't directly reusable: either add an `.sr-compare-panels { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) }` base rule with a `1fr` override in the existing `@media (max-width: 640px)` block in globals.css (the ChecklistComparer's 1fr-1fr grid CAN reuse `.sr-two-col` directly), or skip media queries entirely with inline `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr))`. Also note ACCESSIBILITY.md line 39 currently claims narrow-window reflow 'without clipping content' — it should be corrected or the fix shipped to keep that published statement true.

title: The same 'open this checklist on eBird' function is identified four different ways across tabs
description: One repeated function — a link that opens a specific checklist on ebird.org — is identified with four different affordances and three different name vocabularies depending on the tab (this is the identification inconsistency itself, distinct from the already-reported missing new-window indication and the ↗ accessible-name weakness): (1) bare '↗' glyph with title="Open checklist" (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589); (2) data value + lucide ExternalLink icon, no label at all (speciesDetail/ui.tsx:52-78 StatValueLink, Checklists.tsx:48-65 DateLink) — except NamedBirdRow.tsx:91-100, where the identical id+icon link carries aria-label="Open eBird checklist S… (opens in a new tab)"; (3) plain accent-colored text with no icon and no underline, indistinguishable from the adjacent non-link values (BirdingStats.tsx:500, 695, 726, 1448, 1525; SightingsMap.tsx:67 popup dates; map/TargetMarkers.tsx:104); (4) underlined id text with title="View this checklist on eBird" (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). Where a name exists it is inconsistent F31-style: "Open checklist" vs "View this checklist on eBird" vs "Open eBird checklist S…". A screen-reader user who learns one identification on the Checklists tab cannot recognize the same function on Statistics or in a map popup, and sighted users get no stable visual signature for 'this opens the checklist' either.
evidence: WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111 `{id}` vs BirdingStats.tsx:1332 `↗` vs Checklists.tsx:54-62 `{formatDate(date)}` (no label) vs BirdingStats.tsx:500-505 date-only link with `textDecoration: 'none'` and no icon.
suggestedFix: Create one shared ChecklistLink component (extending the existing speciesDetail/ui.tsx StatValueLink, which already gates on SUBMISSION_ID_RE) with a single visual signature (ExternalLink icon) and one accessible-name formula (e.g. aria-label=`Open checklist ${id} on eBird` plus the new-tab suffix already used in NamedBirdRow). Replace all four variants — the ↗ glyphs, the unlabeled icon links, the plain-text links, and the title-only underlined ids — with it.

verdict.reasoning: All four variants verified at the cited lines: bare ↗ with title='Open checklist' (BirdingStats 1332/1564/1589), value+ExternalLink with no label (StatValueLink ui.tsx:52-78, DateLink Checklists.tsx:48-65) vs NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100's full aria-label, plain accent text with textDecoration:'none' (BirdingStats 500/695/726/1448/1525, SightingsMap.tsx:62-75, TargetMarkers.tsx:104 — which is in fact a fifth vocabulary, 'View checklist S… →'), and underlined id with title='View this checklist on eBird' (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). This is a genuine 3.2.4 inconsistent-identification issue whose root cause (no shared component or name formula) is distinct from confirmed #53 (↗ missing accessible name) and structure findings #4/#5 (new-window indication, title-attribute reliance), which the finding explicitly carves out. The suggested shared ChecklistLink keeps the SUBMISSION_ID_RE standing security check, consistent with conventions.

title: Breeding-code meanings are hover-only: full code labels live solely in title attributes on the Breeding Codes tab and comparer badges
wcag: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus AA (UA-tooltip exemption applies — flagged as the only route to the information)
description: Title-attribute tooltips are user-agent controlled and therefore exempt from 1.4.13 itself, but three locations make the title the ONLY route to what an eBird breeding code abbreviation means, and UA title tooltips never appear on keyboard focus or touch: (1) BreedingCodeTable.tsx:148 — the matrix column headers show only the code (e.g. "NY") with `title={def.label}`; the per-cell sr-only text (line 228) adds only the tier category ("Confirmed"), not the label. (2) BreedingCodeList.tsx:324 — the per-code filter pills, same pattern (`title={def.label}` with the bare code as content). (3) ChecklistComparer.tsx:31-40 — BreedingBadge renders only `def.code` with `title={`${def.code} — ${def.label}`}` and no aria-label. There is no visible legend on the Breeding Codes tab, and docs/HELP.md's Breeding Codes section (line 273+) describes the matrix without listing the 23 codes; the full labels are visible only in Species Detail's per-species breeding section (SpeciesDetail.tsx:~1003), which covers just the codes that one selected species has. Mouse users get the UA tooltip and screen readers get the title as accessible description (name-from-content is the code, title falls back to description), but a sighted keyboard or touch user — including anyone on the self-hosted/tablet path — has no way on these views to learn that "FL" means recently fledged young.
evidence: BreedingCodeTable.tsx:148 `title={def.label}` on a <th> whose visible content is `{code}{sortIndicator(code)}`; BreedingCodeList.tsx:324 `title={def.label}` on the code pill whose content is a color dot + `{code}`; ChecklistComparer.tsx:31 `title={`${def.code} — ${def.label}`}` on a span containing only `{def.code}`; grep finds no other rendering of def.label in those three files and no code legend in docs/HELP.md.
suggestedFix: Add a non-hover route on the Breeding Codes tab: a collapsible "Code legend" disclosure above the matrix listing code → label (one shared component could also serve the comparer), or render the label in each column header at reduced size. Minimal alternative: append the label to each control's accessible name (aria-label={`${code} — ${def.label}`} on the pills/headers, keeping the visible code) and give ChecklistComparer's BreedingBadge the same aria-label — that fixes AT consistency, though a visible legend is what helps sighted touch/keyboard users.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at all three locations: BreedingCodeTable.tsx:148 (th content is just the code, title={def.label}; the per-cell sr-only at :228 adds only the tier category), BreedingCodeList.tsx:324 (pill with title only), and ChecklistComparer.tsx:31 (BreedingBadge, title only — on a non-interactive span, so even AT exposure is unreliable). grep confirms def.label renders nowhere else in those views, docs/HELP.md's Breeding Codes section lists no codes and its comparer section literally says 'Hover for the full code name', and full labels appear only in Species Detail's per-species section. ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'hidden text label' claim covers tier color, not code meaning, so nothing is disclosed; no existing finding overlaps (the confirmed breeding-code items are contrast-only).

title: Comparer media/side-header cells fixed at 132px
description: The per-row media/count cell (`width: 132, flexShrink: 0`, ChecklistComparer.tsx:74) and its matching SideHeader (`width: 132`, :506) are fixed pixel widths holding 0.75rem text and badges. At 200% the cell contents (count + breeding-code badge + media badges) exceed 132px and push into the species-name column. Same family as the Statistics fixed-px finding but a separate file/owner, listed for completeness.
fix: Use a rem width (e.g. '9rem') or `minWidth` so the cell grows with its text; keep header and cell sharing one constant.

verdict.reasoning: Verified width: 132/flexShrink: 0 at line 74, the matching SideHeader 132 at line 506, plus a fixed 34px count box at line 88; lib/textScale.ts scales only rem text (--sr-text-scale up to 2x), so at 200% the rem-sized badge text outgrows the px boxes and a badge-dense row overflows or clips. Cannot be refuted via browser zoom: ACCESSIBILITY.md explicitly claims SC 1.4.4 conformance through the in-app control because the desktop app has no browser zoom, and its only zoom disclosure (horizontal scroll for tables/maps under 1.4.10) does not cover this. Minor is the right severity — localized overlap on the densest rows of one tab.
verdict.fixNote: Prefer a shared rem-width constant (e.g. const SIDE_CELL_WIDTH = '9rem') used by both SideCell and SideHeader over minWidth — minWidth would let per-row cell widths diverge and break the A/B count alignment the fixed width exists for (per the code comment 'Fixed width so counts line up'). Also convert the inner count box at line 88 from width: 34 to a rem value (e.g. '2.25rem'), since it clips 3-digit counts at 200% independently of the cell width.

title: Comment-count live regions announce on every keystroke
description: CommentSearchBox's match count (N comments, used by both the Checklist Comments and Species Comments sections) recomputes from the filter input on every keystroke, so a screen reader queues an "N comments" announcement per character typed, competing with character echo. The count announcement itself is good 4.1.3 practice — it just needs to settle.
fix: Debounce the text feeding the live region (~400-500 ms after typing pauses) while leaving the visible count immediate.

verdict.reasoning: Checklists.tsx:177 puts aria-live="polite" on the count span, and matches recomputes synchronously from the filter input (useMemo on filter, set in onChange), so every count-changing keystroke mutates the live region and queues an announcement over character echo — used by both comment sections. Slight overstatement ('every keystroke' is really 'every keystroke that changes the count') but substantively correct, and minor is the right severity. ACCESSIBILITY.md mentions polite count regions as a feature, not this chattiness as a known issue, so not already disclosed.
verdict.fixNote: The visible count and the live region are the same span, so a naive debounce would also lag the visible count. Split them: keep the existing visible span immediate but add aria-hidden, and render a visually-hidden sibling with aria-live="polite" fed by a ~400-500 ms debounced copy of the count text (debounced state via useEffect + setTimeout keyed on matches.length). Apply the same pattern to the line 668 checklist-count region, which has the same shape (though it is mostly click-driven, the date inputs can also type-churn it).

title: The 'loading-saved' phase on four data tabs is a bare unlabeled spinner — nothing is announced and nothing names the state
wcag: 4.1.3 Status Messages AA (also 1.1.1 Non-text Content A)
description: While a tab parses the stored CSV (the phase every visit passes through before the data or the SetupRequired panel appears), four tabs replace their entire panel with a centered Loader2 SVG and nothing else: Checklists.tsx:468-470 (the icon is even explicitly aria-hidden, leaving zero accessible content in the panel), LifeList.tsx:362-364, SpeciesDetail.tsx:408-410, and BreedingCodeList.tsx:174-176. There is no role="status", no aria-label, and no visible text, so a screen-reader user lands in an empty tabpanel with no indication anything is happening. Every other loading state in the app does this correctly and was recorded as a pass (boot skeleton role=status 'Loading SnowRaven', App.tsx TabLoading role=status with text, BirdingStats.tsx:464 computing status, SnowMap style placeholder) — these four bare spinners are the stragglers. Distinct from prior finding i=74 (which covers role=status nodes that mount with text already present — these have no status semantics at all).
evidence: Checklists.tsx:469 `<Loader2 size={24} strokeWidth={2} className="spin" style={{ color: 'var(--sr-accent)' }} aria-hidden />` as the sole child of the phase's wrapper div; identical Loader2-only blocks at LifeList.tsx:363, SpeciesDetail.tsx:409, BreedingCodeList.tsx:~176 (those three without even aria-hidden, but with no text either).
suggestedFix: Give each wrapper div role="status" and an aria-label (e.g. 'Loading saved eBird data') — or add visible text next to the spinner as WeatherTidePanel does ('Loading weather…') — and keep the SVG aria-hidden, matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern.

verdict.reasoning: All four cited blocks verified: Checklists.tsx:466-472 (Loader2 with aria-hidden as the panel's sole content), LifeList.tsx:360-366, SpeciesDetail.tsx:406-412, BreedingCodeList.tsx:172-178 — no role='status', no aria-label, no text, leaving an empty tabpanel during the loading-saved phase every visit passes through. Genuinely distinct from confirmed i=74, which covers nodes that already have role='status' but mount with text present; these have no status semantics at all. Not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md and not present in either findings file.
verdict.fixNote: Matching the App.tsx TabLoading pattern (role='status' + label on the wrapper, SVG aria-hidden) is right; note per confirmed finding i=74 that a status node mounting with its label may still not be announced by all SRs, but it at least names the state for users who land in the panel — fixing both together would mean mounting the empty status container first and inserting the label.

title: Light theme: error text on error background is just below AA (4.41:1)
description: --sr-error #DC2626 on --sr-error-bg #FEF2F2 computes to 4.41:1 — marginally under 4.5:1 — and this pair styles every error banner and the 'negative' filter pill state: Checklists.tsx:236/488, LifeList.tsx:108/384, BreedingCodeList.tsx:196, Settings.tsx:304/480, ChecklistComparer.tsx:374, NamedBirds.tsx:108, WeatherTidePanel.tsx:186, SpeciesDetail.tsx:430, DropZone.tsx error text. Dark theme passes (7.07:1). Error on plain surface also passes (4.83:1), so only the tinted-banner pair needs a nudge.
fix: Darken light --sr-error slightly (e.g. #D31F1F ≈ 4.8:1 on #FEF2F2) or introduce an --sr-error-text token used on --sr-error-bg; one token edit in globals.css fixes all listed locations.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the pair co-occurs (Checklists.tsx:236 TriPill 'no' state and :488 error banner, plus the other listed files) and re-computed the ratio: #DC2626 on #FEF2F2 = 4.415:1, a genuine but marginal AA miss at 13px text; dark theme (7.07:1) and plain-surface (4.83:1) pass as the finding states. The 0.085 shortfall is perceptually negligible and light-theme-only, so 'moderate' overstates user impact — this is a compliance nudge, not a barrier; downgrading to minor. The fix is validated (#D31F1F = 4.82:1 on #FEF2F2, 5.27:1 on white) and convention-compliant as a single light-theme token edit in globals.css.

title: External links open new windows without any indication (inconsistent across the app)
description: 43 target="_blank" anchors exist across ~20 component files; only two indicate the behavior — App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 use "(opens in new tab)" in aria-label. All others give no warning, including every link in the Help documentation (HelpDocs.tsx:61 renders all HELP.md links with target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" and no indication), the footer GitHub link (App.tsx:1101-1110), SpeciesLinks.tsx:20/45 (whose aria-labels "View X on eBird" omit it), LifeListTable.tsx media-count links, BirdingStats.tsx checklist/region links (15 instances), Checklists.tsx, MapExplorer.tsx, SpeciesDetail.tsx, NamedBirdRow.tsx, Settings.tsx, WeatherTidePanel.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx, MediaStatsSections.tsx, ChecklistComparer.tsx, SightingsMap.tsx, map/HotspotMarkers.tsx, map/TargetMarkers.tsx, AtlasLayer.tsx, speciesDetail/ui.tsx, CommentText.tsx. Unexpected context changes disorient screen-reader and cognitive-disability users; the app already has the right pattern in two places — it just isn't applied consistently.
evidence: HelpDocs.tsx:61 `<a key={ki++} href={lm[2]} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` with no new-window indication; grep shows 43 target="_blank" instances, only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 carry "(opens in new tab)".
suggestedFix: Adopt one shared ExternalA component (or extend SpeciesLinks' pattern) that appends "(opens in new tab)" to the accessible name (visually-hidden span or aria-label suffix) and use it for all target="_blank" anchors, including HelpDocs' renderInline link branch.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by grep: exactly 43 target="_blank" anchors across 20 component files, with only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 announcing '(opens in new tab)'; HelpDocs.tsx renders every documentation link target="_blank" with no indication and SpeciesLinks.tsx aria-labels omit it. This is the new-window-indication aspect, explicitly distinct from confirmed #53 (which covers the ↗ links' accessible names), so not a duplicate. Correctly scoped as advisory (G201; 3.2.5 is AAA), so minor severity is right; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: A shared external-link component is sound; prefer a visually-hidden span suffix over aria-label so existing link text is preserved, and where an aria-label already exists (SpeciesLinks, icon-only links) append to the label, matching the wording already used at App.tsx:748/898. For icon-only favicon links keep title in sync with the label.

title: Zero-result filter state in Multimedia and Breeding Codes renders a header-only empty table with no 'no results' message (Checklists has one)
wcag: 4.1.3 Status Messages AA (best-practice gap; the only signal is the count label)
description: Runtime-verified: with a filter that matches nothing (From=2099-01-01), the Multimedia and Breeding Codes tabs render their full column-header row above a zero-row tbody with no visible or accessible 'no results match these filters' message anywhere in the panel (probe found 0 tbody rows and zero empty-state text nodes on both tabs). The only indication is the small count label ('0 of N species' — and on Multimedia that label is currently wrong, see the companion finding). The Checklists tab is the in-house model: it renders the explicit text 'No checklists match these filters.' (Checklists.tsx:705) distinct from its empty-data message, and MediaCommentsSection has emptyAll/emptyFiltered props. Locations: LifeListTable.tsx:253-254 (`<tbody>{sorted.map(…)}` with no empty branch) and BreedingCodeTable.tsx:253-area tbody (same pattern; its filter at BreedingCodeTable.tsx:29 can yield an empty `filtered`).
evidence: Runtime probe on both tabs with From=2099-01-01: `{"tableRows":0, "tablePresent":true, "emptyMsg":[]}`; Checklists in the same state showed `"emptyMsg":["No checklists match these filters."]` plus the announced count '0 of 3,163 checklists'.
suggestedFix: When the sorted/filtered row set is empty, render a single full-width cell (or a div below the table) with the Checklists wording — 'No species match these filters.' vs 'No species found in the stored file.' — in --sr-text-muted, in both LifeListTable and BreedingCodeTable. The existing aria-live count label then announces the change while the visible message explains it.

verdict.reasoning: Code-verified: LifeListTable.tsx:253 (<tbody>{sorted.map(...)}) and BreedingCodeTable.tsx:164 (same pattern; its filter at line 29 can empty 'filtered') have no empty-row branch, and BreedingCodeList's only empty message (line 220) is gated on !hasLocationFilter, so a filtered-to-zero state renders a header-only table with no explanation. Checklists.tsx:705 renders the explicit 'No checklists match these filters.' message, so the inconsistency is real. Fairly flagged as a minor best-practice gap; no duplicate exists in either findings file.
verdict.fixNote: Minor line correction: BreedingCodeTable's tbody is at lines 164-165, not ~253. Suggested fix is convention-compliant (--sr-text-muted exists in both themes); a full-width <td colSpan={...}> inside the tbody keeps the table structure valid.

title: Comparison-mode switch uses tablist/tab roles without panels or arrow-key support
description: The Life Lists / Checklists mode switch is role="tablist" + role="tab" aria-selected, but there is no aria-controls, no role="tabpanel" for the swapped content, no roving tabindex, and no arrow-key handling — SR users are told they're in a tab widget whose conventions (arrows move, panel follows) don't hold. Inside the app shell's real tab system, this also nests tab semantics within a tabpanel.
fix: Either complete the pattern (ids + aria-controls + tabpanel + roving tabindex + arrows) or simplify to a role="group" of aria-pressed buttons like SortSeg.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at ListComparer.tsx:150-165: role=tablist/tab with aria-selected but no aria-controls, no tabpanel on the swapped content (line 168), both tabs tabIndex={0} (no roving), and no onKeyDown anywhere in the file. The nesting claim also holds — App.tsx mounts ListComparer inside the id=panel-comparer role=tabpanel. Keyboard operation still works via Tab+Enter on the real buttons, so minor is the correct severity; ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose this (it asserts the main tab bar follows the standard arrow-key pattern), and the suggested SortSeg-style role=group/aria-pressed fix matches the existing convention in Checklists.tsx.

title: WCAG 2.2 forward-looking: several form controls are under the 24px minimum target size
description: Forward-looking 2.2 delta only. The atlas overlay role="switch" buttons are 38x22px (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under the 24px minimum), and several zero-padding text buttons are ~16-18px tall: the API-key Show/Hide button (Settings.tsx:363-373, padding 0, 0.75rem text), the 'Clear filter' underline buttons (LifeList.tsx:694-703, Checklists.tsx:685-690, SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667), and the 'Go to Settings →' banner buttons (App.tsx:611-619, padding 0). Most currently escape 2.5.8 via the spacing exception (no adjacent target within 24px), but that is fragile under layout changes and the small targets are already hard for motor-impaired users under 2.1 best practice.
fix: Bump the switch buttons to at least 24px tall (e.g. 44x24 track) and give the zero-padding text buttons enough padding (or min-height: 24px with negative-margin compensation) to reach a 24x24 hit area.

verdict.reasoning: All cited controls verified: the three hand-rolled role=switch buttons are 38x22 (MapExplorer.tsx:726, :759, :788 — 22px tall, under 24), and the padding-0 text buttons exist as described in Settings.tsx:363-373 (Show/Hide), LifeList.tsx:694-703 / Checklists.tsx:685-690 / SpeciesDetail.tsx:658-667 (Clear filter), and App.tsx:611-619 (Go to Settings), all at 0.75rem with no padding (~17px hit height). The finding honestly frames itself as a forward-looking WCAG 2.2 delta and acknowledges the spacing exception currently covers most of them, so minor is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The codebase already has a shared ui/ToggleSwitch.tsx (a 30px-tall role=switch button with the label inside) — prefer migrating the three inline atlas switches to it, or if the label-left/switch-right layout must stay, bump the bare track to >=24px tall (e.g. 44x24). For the zero-padding text buttons, padding (or min-height 24 with negative-margin compensation) as originally suggested is fine.

title: Map Explorer Filters accordion button lacks aria-expanded
description: The collapsible filter panel toggle in the sightings sidebar (button at :836, panel collapsed via max-height 0) exposes no expanded/collapsed state — the only cue is the rotated chevron. Every other disclosure in the app does carry aria-expanded (NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76/:440, TabNav.tsx:234).
fix: Add aria-expanded={filterOpen} (and optionally aria-controls) to the Filters button.

verdict.reasoning: The Filters disclosure button (MapExplorer.tsx:835-847) carries no aria-expanded; the only state cue is the rotated ChevronDown, and the panel collapses via maxHeight 0. Verified the cited convention claim: NamedBirdRow.tsx:36, ChecklistComparer.tsx:76 and :440, and TabNav.tsx:234 all set aria-expanded on their disclosures, so this is an isolated omission. Minor is right and the suggested one-attribute fix (aria-expanded={filterOpen}, optionally aria-controls) is correct and conventional.

title: Date-range filter is a native date picker on four tabs but free-text 'YYYY-MM-DD' fields on Map Explorer
wcag: 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA) — advisory; primarily a consistency/usability gap
description: The identical 'filter sightings by date range' function is presented and identified two different ways. Life List (LifeList.tsx:644-669), Breeding Codes (BreedingCodeList.tsx:408-419), Species Detail (SpeciesDetail.tsx:629-654), and Checklists (Checklists.tsx:653-667) all use paired <input type="date"> controls — native picker UI, a Calendar icon, an accent-fill active state, and a '→' separator. Map Explorer alone implements the same function as two <input type="text"> fields whose only identification is the placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD' (MapExplorer.tsx:862-865), under a 'Date Range' sidebar label. A user who has learned the app-wide date-picker idiom reaches the map and must instead hand-type ISO dates with no picker, no format validation affordance, and no visible from/to distinction (the indistinguishable naming is already reported; this finding is the cross-tab inconsistency of widget and identification). The interaction divergence is not a strict 3.2.4 failure (3.2.4 governs identification, and the labels that do exist don't conflict), so this is recorded as an advisory consistency defect with real cognitive-accessibility cost.
evidence: MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 `<input type="text" placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" value={dateFrom} …/><input type="text" placeholder="YYYY-MM-DD" value={dateTo} …/>` vs LifeList.tsx:644-647 `<input type="date" value={dateRange.from} …/>` (same pattern on BreedingCodeList.tsx:408, SpeciesDetail.tsx:629, Checklists.tsx:653).
suggestedFix: Switch the Map Explorer sidebar date fields to the same paired <input type="date"> pattern used everywhere else (with the From/To accessible names the prior audit already calls for); keep the visible 'Date Range' SidebarLabel, which the other tabs could in fact adopt.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: MapExplorer.tsx:862-865 uses two <input type="text"> with only a 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder under one 'Date Range' label, while LifeList.tsx:644, BreedingCodeList.tsx:408, SpeciesDetail.tsx:629, and Checklists.tsx:653 all use paired <input type="date"> (one evidence overstatement: Checklists' pair has no Calendar icon or accent-fill active state — those three trimmings are on the other three tabs only, but the core text-vs-native-picker divergence holds). The advisory framing is fair — same function, different widget and identification, with real cognitive/motor cost from hand-typing ISO dates. Distinct aspect and fix from confirmed #56/#59, which cover the accessible-name/placeholder problem on the same inputs.
verdict.fixNote: Switching to type="date" also moots the 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder-as-name issue from #56/#59 — apply the From/To aria-labels (as Checklists.tsx:655/663 already does) in the same change.

title: Inline `outline: 'none'` on ~20 inputs/selects suppresses the designed focus ring app-wide
description: One repeated pattern: form controls styled with inline `outline: 'none'`, which overrides the global input ring (globals.css:556-563, `outline: 2px solid var(--sr-accent)`). The only surviving indicator is the rule's `border-color: var(--sr-accent) !important` (stylesheet !important still beats inline) plus a 12%-alpha shadow — a 1.5px gray→green border tint instead of the designed 2px ring, easy to miss in dense filter sidebars, and weaker than ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs'. Locations: lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:27 (SELECT_STYLE shared by all Map Explorer selects); MapExplorer.tsx:88,690,692,863,865,1184; LifeList.tsx:627,653,667; BreedingCodeList.tsx:388,419,435; SpeciesDetail.tsx:518,613,638,652,1273; Checklists.tsx:170,265; MediaCommentsSection.tsx:75; Settings.tsx:435,1219,1231,1243. Technically still a visible state change (so not a hard 2.4.7 fail), but a significant app-wide degradation versus the global design.
fix: Remove every inline `outline: 'none'` from inputs/selects — the global stylesheet already suppresses the default ring on non-focus-visible states and supplies the 2px accent ring on focus. The per-element onFocus borderColor handlers (e.g. Settings.tsx:437) become redundant and can stay or go.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all claims: 26 inline outline:'none' occurrences match the listed locations, inline style beats the non-!important outline in globals.css:556-563, and only the !important border-color plus the stylesheet box-shadow survive — the designed 2px ring never renders on these controls. However the surviving indicator (1.5px border flipping gray→accent at 4.52:1 light / 9.22:1 dark vs surface, plus a 4px glow, with explicit onFocus borderColor handlers in Settings) is a perceivable, conventional focus treatment, so 2.4.7 AA is not actually failed — the finding itself concedes this. Real as an app-wide design-consistency issue that also makes ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs' claim inaccurate, but a non-failing degradation grades as minor, not moderate.

title: Southern-hemisphere moon emoji mirroring makes screen readers announce the wrong phase
description: The moon-phase emoji is the ONLY carrier of moon-phase information in night weather blocks (no adjacent text line — the condition emoji, by contrast, is followed by the textual condition on the next line). For northern latitudes this is acceptable: SRs read Unicode emoji names ("waxing gibbous moon"), which match the phase. But MOON_SOUTH deliberately swaps to the visually-mirrored emoji for lat < 0, so a southern-hemisphere waxing crescent is rendered as 🌘 whose Unicode name is "waning crescent moon" — a SR (and anyone hovering for the character name) hears the opposite phase. Constrained by the paste-into-eBird output format, so an in-app-only fix is appropriate.
fix: Where the formatted block is displayed in-app (the <pre> on the Weather tab and WeatherTidePanel), wrap the header emoji run in a span with an aria-label giving the true phase name (e.g. "cloudy, waxing crescent moon"), or append the phase as text in the in-app rendering only.

verdict.reasoning: weatherFormatter.ts:93-102 swaps to mirrored emoji for lat<0, so all six asymmetric phases carry the opposite phase's Unicode name (verified: southern waxing crescent emits 🌘 'waning crescent moon'); the emoji is the block's only phase carrier (formatWeatherBody emits `${emoji}${moon}` with no phase text line) and renders as raw text in the Weather tab <pre> (App.tsx:827) and WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock, where SRs announce it by character name. ACCESSIBILITY.md does not disclose this — it actually claims icon-only info carries hidden text labels. Minor is fair: narrow trigger (southern hemisphere + night checklist + SR) but the announced info is actively wrong, a genuine 1.1.1 failure.
verdict.fixNote: In the in-app renderings only (App.tsx Weather-tab <pre> ~line 811 and WeatherTidePanel's MonoBlock), split off the header line and wrap the emoji run in <span role="img" aria-label="..."> — a bare span aria-label is not reliably honored by SRs without role="img". Derive the true phase name by exporting it from weatherFormatter.ts (e.g. a moonPhaseName(unixTs) beside moonPhaseEmoji, or reverse-lookup the rendered emoji's index in MOON_SOUTH when lat < 0; northern emoji names are already correct). Do NOT change formatWeatherBody's output string — it is byte-locked with backend/formatters/weather.py and the commentBlocks.ts stripper anchors on the unspaced contiguous emoji run.
